assertions.name: q_beta_reference_is_truncated_to_eight_figures
assertions.source: codata_constants.Q_BETA_MEV = 0.7823334099999999999999999999999999999999999999999994098296040398407753 differs from the witness's own reference by 8.8209e-10 — a truncated reference in a corpus that computes at 60 dps. Recorded, not fixed.

description: The corpus establishes (qou-e58e, 11 nuclei, five q) that bar: q -> 1/q IS proton<->neutron conjugation, and at bond level p<->n is exactly z<->zbar. Q_beta's element Delta = B_n - B_p is a p<->n DIFFERENCE, so under that conjugation it should be bar-ODD: bar(tr_M(Delta)) = -tr_M(Delta). Tested on the two candidate elements the fork leaves open. Delta_S (normal-form difference, tr_M AFFINE in z): bar-odd iff bar(z) = z - h, ONE branch, satisfied by EXACTLY the two admissible functionals (z=q augmentation, z_D = q^3/(q^2+1)) and by neither z=1 (published) nor z_C (excised C). Delta_L (eleven-crossing word difference, tr_M QUADRATIC in z): two branches, satisfied by NONE of the four, the admissible pair included. So under the isospin reading Delta_S + admissible functional is bar-odd and Delta_L + admissible functional is not — a structural preference for Delta_S in a question the decision document records as open, reached with NO anchor and NO experimental input. SCOPE-(a), NOT (b): Delta_L is NOT excluded. Its first branch bar(z) = -z is vacuous for positive z, but the second is involution-consistent (Bbar(B(z)) - z = 0 identically), so a solution may exist and none was searched for. Nothing wired, no functional adopted, no element declared canonical.

scope.established: Delta_S is bar-odd under EXACTLY the two admissible functionals; Delta_L is bar-odd under NONE of the four tested, the admissible pair included
scope.NOT_established: that Delta_L can never be bar-odd — its second branch is involution-consistent, so a solution z(q) may exist and none was searched for
scope.premise: bar is p<->n conjugation, measured in qou-e58e over 11 nuclei; a p<->n DIFFERENCE should therefore be bar-odd. If that reading is wrong, the criterion loses its motivation and this becomes an observation about two rational functions.
